what_it_does.name: neon-postgres
what_it_does.summary: Instructions and six reference documents for working with Lakebase Postgres on Neon, with no bundled scripts. They cover choosing pooled or direct connections and drivers, branching, migrations, computes, autoscaling, scale to zero, instant restore, read replicas and Neon-specific diagnostics through the neon CLI or the Neon MCP server. The references add branch workflows, a four-step egress optimization procedure and Lakebase Search setup for vector, full-text and hybrid search, with SQL and TypeScript examples. Use it when the work is an existing DATABASE_URL, SQL, schema, inspection or search on Neon.
tasks: pick pooled or direct connections and a driver
create normal or schema-only branches and reset a branch from its parent
diagnose performance with neon inspect db checks
manage computes, autoscaling and scale to zero
find and fix query patterns that cause high egress
set up vector, full-text and hybrid search with Lakebase Search
covers the Neon access path to Lakebase Postgres, not the Databricks one
what_it_does.author_description: Guides and best practices for working with Lakebase Postgres on Neon: connections, pooled vs direct, schema migrations, branching (including schema-only, reset-from-parent, and branch-per-PR workflows), autoscaling, scale-to-zero, instant restore, read replicas, IP allow lists, logical replication, egress optimization, and Lakebase Search. Use when the work is an existing DATABASE_URL, SQL, schema, inspect, or search. New backends, Auth, files, Functions, and LLM calls go to the parent `neon` skill. Live queries, reactive UIs, and realtime data go to `neon-realtime`. Also use for "@neondatabase/serverless", "@neon/neon-js", "neon inspect db", "neon postgres computes", "Neon branch", "schema-only branch", "reset branch", "branch per PR", high database bills, network transfer or egress, SELECT * optimization, query overfetching, "semantic search", "vector search", "full-text search", "BM25", or "hybrid search".

risks.risk: Instructions hidden in user-supplied SQL, schema definitions, code or .env files reach an agent that can run neon CLI commands, write .env and execute SQL.
risks.mitigation: none for boundary markers, C2 notes that parameterized queries and ORM migrations are recommended

risks.risk: Database connection strings with credentials are read from and written to .env, where an overwrite can lose an existing value.
risks.mitigation: read .env before modifying it and never overwrite an existing key without explicit confirmation, stated in the files

risks.risk: Resetting a child branch from its parent replaces its schema and data, and local changes on the child branch are lost.
Dropping indexes that unused-indexes lists, or running VACUUM FULL or REINDEX on a bloat estimate, can harm the workload or take locks.
risks.mitigation: confirm the observation window, constraints and workload and plan locks first, stated in the files

risks.risk: EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes the statement, so running it on mutating SQL changes data.
risks.mitigation: do not run it autonomously for mutating SQL, stated in the files

risks.risk: A normal branch copies production rows, including sensitive data, into a development or test environment.
risks.mitigation: schema-only branches or an anonymized parent branch, recommended in the files

risks.risk: The parent neon skill fetched from https://neon.com/docs/ai/skills/neon/SKILL.md is loaded without a pinned version or hash, so its instructions can change between runs.
Document bodies and query text leave the machine to the Neon AI Gateway when embeddings are generated or results are reranked with Jev.

limitations: Only child branches can be reset from parent, a branch with children cannot be reset, and reset may be unavailable for up to 24 hours after a parent is restored from snapshot.
Root branch allowances and per-branch storage limits can cap how many schema-only branches users can create.
The first query after suspend typically has a cold-start penalty of around hundreds of ms.
Cache and Postgres statistics reset when compute restarts, including scale-to-zero suspension.
outliers and calls require pg_stat_statements, and lfc-hit-rate and working-set require the neon extension.
The MCP explain_sql_statement tool does not expose the FILECACHE or PREFETCH options.
Free cannot change the suspend timeout, and Launch can only enable or disable suspension.
Lakebase Search requires Postgres 16 or later.
Drizzle cannot express CREATE EXTENSION, and BM25 has no Drizzle helper.
Each Jev request must fit Jev 1.14's 65,536-token context window.

known_problems.problem: migrations, dumps or replication fail over the pooled connection, for example prepared statement "s0" already exists
known_problems.workaround: use the direct DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED, for Prisma through directUrl

known_problems.problem: one failing database fails an all-databases inspection
known_problems.workaround: retry the check with an explicit databaseName

known_problems.problem: unexpected behavior or errors with schema-only branches
known_problems.workaround: share feedback in the Neon Console or open a support conversation in the Neon Discord

known_problems.problem: pg_stat_statements is empty after the compute scaled to zero
known_problems.workaround: after asking, reset the stats and let representative traffic run for at least an hour

known_problems.problem: an AI Gateway model shows enabled: false
known_problems.workaround: the branch's AI Gateway page in the Neon Console lists the reason and the fix

known_problems.problem: the OpenAI SDK v6 base64 decoder can turn float arrays into zeros
a numeric lakebase_ann.probes value that does not match lists errors
known_problems.workaround: keep probes at 'auto' unless an IVF lists layout exists

known_problems.problem: drizzle-kit push drops the post-seed lakebase_bm25 index

known_problems.workaround: catch the error and fall back to RRF
